messages.text: Alpine condemn online abuse since Colapinto crash, Norris remarks

metadata.summary: Alpine have condemned the online abuse and hate aimed at drivers and others in Formula 1 since the incident in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that saw Franco Colapinto cause a three-car collision with Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris.
metadata.content: Alpine condemn online abuse since Franco Colapinto three-car Azerbaijan GP crash with Pierre Gasly, Lando Norris | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Update Alpine condemn online abuse since Franco Colapinto three-car Azerbaijan GP crash with Pierre Gasly, Lando Norris Franco Colapinto's mistake at first Safety Car restart in Baku led to chain-reaction accident that also saw team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris drop out; Alpine condemn social media abuse aimed at all sides seen since crash Sunday 27 September 2026 14:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was carnage on the safety car restart after contact between Alpine team-mates resulted in Lando Norris crashing out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix Alpine have condemned the online abuse and hate aimed at drivers and others in Formula 1 since the incident in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that saw Franco Colapinto cause a three-car collision with Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris. Alpine driver Colapinto triggered the accident in the Baku race's first Safety Car restart when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of team-mate Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside. "Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport," Alpine said as part of a statement issued on Sunday.
